bib.title: Visual Genome: Connecting Language and Vision Using Crowdsourced Dense Image Annotations

read.skipped: Reference list after the first entries only skimmed; no appendices exist.

question: Can a dataset of densely crowdsourced region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships and QA pairs support cognitive image-understanding tasks beyond object recognition?
hypothesis: Models need to understand relationships between objects, so training data should annotate them densely rather than only label objects or give one caption per image.
contributions: Dense annotation of 108,077 images: region descriptions, objects, attributes, relationships, region graphs, scene graphs and QA pairs
Canonicalization of objects, attributes, relationships and noun phrases to WordNet synsets
Baseline experiments on attribute prediction, relationship prediction, region captioning and QA

method.summary: Crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk wrote region descriptions with boxes, then extracted objects, attributes and relationships and wrote QA pairs, with verification and WordNet canonicalization. Baselines: fine-tuned VGG-16 plus SVMs for attributes and relationships, NeuralTalk for region captioning, an answer-frequency baseline for QA.
method.task: dataset construction plus baseline attribute, relationship, region-captioning and QA experiments

datasets.name: Visual Genome
datasets.size: 108,077 images; 5,406,939 region descriptions; 3,843,636 objects; 1,773,258 QA pairs
datasets.split: attributes/relationships: 80/10/10 by image; region captioning: 3,784,857 train, 811,040 val, 811,040 test, split by image; QA: 60% train / 40% test, split by image
datasets.source: Creative Commons intersection of MS-COCO (328,000) and YFCC100M (100 million) images; open access CC BY 4.0 paper
datasets.preprocessing: Attribute and relationship experiments: lowercase, lemmatize, strip whitespace, top 100 attributes or relationships, at most 500 samples per class. Region captions: strip non-alphanumerics, lowercase.

datasets.name: Flickr30K
datasets.preprocessing: Baseline captioner for comparison; Table 8 labels this row Flickr8K

models.name: VGG 16-layer (fine-tuned)
models.architecture: CNN, 16 layers, ImageNet pretrained, SVM head (100 SVMs)

other.input: crop of object box (attributes) or union box of subject and object (relationships)

models.name: Answer-frequency baseline
models.architecture: predicts top-k most frequent training answers (k = 100, 500, 1000)

training.optimizer: VGG fine-tune: not named, momentum 0.9; NeuralTalk: rmsprop
training.lr: VGG: 0.001 base, final FC layer 10x; NeuralTalk: 0.001
training.steps: attribute: converges after around 700 iterations; object-attribute: around 400; relationship: around 800; relationship+objects: around 450
training.wall_clock: NeuralTalk region model converges after four days

other.svm: 100 individual SVMs on fine-tuned features, one per attribute

inference.samples: single run per experiment; no seeds stated

other.region_caption_eval: ground-truth region boxes cropped, 4096-d VGG features fed to NeuralTalk; outputs converted to full sentences with templates (Hou et al. 2002)

metrics.name: Top-1 / Top-5 accuracy
metrics.definition: correct label among top 1 or 5 predictions (attribute, relationship)

metrics.name: Human correctness
metrics.definition: crowd workers judge whether a generated description is correct

metrics.name: QA top-k accuracy
metrics.definition: correct if one of k frequent-answer predictions exactly matches the ground-truth answer

metrics.name: Human QA
metrics.definition: image, question and 10 multiple-choice answers (1 true, 9 random)

baselines: NeuralTalk trained on Flickr30K vs Visual Genome
eval.protocol: No seeds or significance tests for the baselines; a t-test is reported only for semantic cluster diversity (t = -240, p < 0.01).

results.claim: Visual Genome region descriptions are more semantically diverse than MS-COCO captions: about 17 clusters of 71 per image (4 vs 2 with 5 sampled descriptions, t = -240, p < 0.01).
results.setup: word2vec 300-d averaged vectors, hierarchical agglomerative clustering into 71 clusters; all 50 descriptions. With 5 random descriptions: 4 clusters vs 2 for COCO (t = -240, p < 0.01).
results.note: Value left null: the 17 appears across a line break in the text.

limits: Annotations are not exhaustive: correct predictions can be scored wrong because the ground truth lacks valid attributes (Sect 6.1, Sect 7).
Images are biased toward people and sports; twice as many annotations for men as for women.
93.02% of crowd workers were in the US.
Baselines are 2015-era (VGG-16 plus SVMs, NeuralTalk, frequency counting) and are not tuned or run with seeds.
The QA exact-match metric works poorly for long answers.
